column2: Hiked Precipice this morning. Rungs were icy near the top, would not do it without microspikes until it warms up.
Lake Marie trail still snowed in above 10,500 ft. Postholing past the second switchback, bring snowshoes.
Heads up: the footbridge over the Swift River on the Mt Tom trail is out. Crossing was knee deep after yesterday's rain.
Blowdown everywhere on the Bigelow Range trail after Tuesday's wind. Counted 30+ trees between Horns Pond and the col.
Trail conditions update: Angel's Landing chains are dry, crowds light before 8am, permit checked at Scout Lookout.
Mud season is real on the Long Trail. Ankle deep from Route 17 to the shelter, please stay on the treadway.
Just got back from Medicine Bow Peak. Trail clear of snow, wind was brutal on the summit ridge, 40+ mph gusts.
Road to the trailhead is washed out 2 miles below the lot. Had to park at the gate and walk up.
Mosquitoes are horrendous at Titcomb Basin right now. Headnets essential, trail itself in great shape.
The Katahdin Hunt Trail is closed today due to high winds per the ranger at Katahdin Stream.
Water crossing at Wildcat Brook was waist high this afternoon, we turned around. Give it a few dry days.
Kings Peak summit today via Henry's Fork. Some lingering snow on Gunsight Pass but easy to walk around.
Trailhead lot was full by 7:15 am on Saturday, overflow parking on the shoulder being ticketed.
Ice on the Franconia Ridge this morning, the rocks near Little Haystack were glazed. Spikes and poles needed.
Went up Mount Washington via Tuckerman Ravine, the headwall trail is closed for the season, used Lion Head.
Smoke from the fire north of us made visibility poor on the Teton Crest today, air quality felt bad by noon.
Delicate Arch trail is fine but the slickrock was super hot by 11. Bring more water than you think.
Several trees down across the Beehive trail after the storm, passable with some scrambling around them.
Snowbridges on the Wind River approach are getting sketchy, stream audible under them. Crossed early.
Fresh rockfall on the trail below the saddle, a few large blocks in the path. Watch your step.
Bugs were bad at the lake but the trail was dry all the way to the pass. Wildflowers peaking.
Section of the Appalachian Trail near Dragon's Tooth is rerouted, follow the orange flagging.
Avalanche debris across the summer trail at mile 3. Firm in the morning, soft by afternoon.
Trail report: Old Rag rock scramble dry, line at the chimney about 20 minutes around noon.
The creek crossing on the Hellroaring trail is running high and fast with snowmelt. Unsafe to ford today.
Grinnell Glacier trail open to the lake as of this morning, snow on the last half mile, poles helpful.
Got to the Chimney Pond trailhead and the road was closed at Roaring Brook for washout repairs.
Just a note that the switchbacks on the east side are severely eroded after the storms. Loose gravel, slow going.
Summit of Timp this morning. Snowfield below the saddle is still there and firm early, ice axe recommended.
Parking lot at the Cascade Pass trailhead is full, cars parked a quarter mile down the road.
Microspikes were enough today on the Mount Monadnock White Dot trail, ice under light snow on the ledges.
Hiked the Narrows bottom up this morning. Water was thigh deep and cold, flow was about 60 cfs.
Blowdowns cleared on the Hamilton Mountain trail, thanks to the crew. Trail in good shape now.
The upper trail is covered in slick mud and roots, took us twice as long as usual.
Bear activity reported at the campground, rangers closed sites 12 to 20. Trail still open.
Trail to the fire tower is officially closed for bridge repair, detour via the north loop adds a mile.
Wind chill near zero on the ridge today, rime ice on every cairn. Full winter gear needed above treeline.
Chains on Angels Landing were icy this morning, rangers were turning people back at Scout Lookout.
Spring runoff has the Big Cottonwood trail flooded in a couple spots, waterproof boots recommended.
Went up Pikes Peak via Barr Trail today. Snow above Barr Camp, packed out and fine with spikes.
Downed tree blocking the trail at mile 1.8, you can climb over but not with a heavy pack.
Trailhead gate at Moose Brook is locked until May 15, add 1.5 miles of road walking.
Rattlesnake on the trail near the second overlook this afternoon, keep an eye out.
Did the Enchantments thru today. Aasgard Pass loose and dry, snow gone from the core zone.
Beaver dam flooding on the lower trail, the boardwalk is under a foot of water.
Summit trail is a sheet of ice from treeline up. Turned around at the second cairn. Crampons, not spikes.
The Huckleberry trail had a lot of washouts after last night's thunderstorm. Bridge at the creek is fine.
Snowmobiles have packed the trail to the pond, easy walking with spikes this weekend.
Hiking the Presidential traverse today, cloud cap and 50 mph winds on Madison, we bailed via Valley Way.
Found the trail markers painted over for the reroute near the quarry. Signs are posted at both ends.
Trail crews working on the Skyline trail this week, expect short delays near the stairs.
The Half Dome cables are down for the season as of today.
Heavy snow overnight, about 8 inches at the trailhead and more above. Nobody has broken trail yet.
Muddy and wet on the lower half, dry and dusty above the junction. Lots of hikers today.
Fording the North Fork was chest deep, not recommended. Took the high route instead.
Poison ivy has overgrown the first half mile of the river trail, long pants recommended.
Water source at the spring is dry. Carry everything you need from the trailhead.
Stairs on the Mist Trail are wet and slippery with spray from the falls, take it slow.
The ladders on the Beehive are solid, but the rungs near the top were wet with fog this morning.
Tick check after the meadow section, picked off four on the way back to the car.
Rim trail closed between the two viewpoints because of rockfall, rangers posted signs.
Horse flies relentless near the marsh, otherwise trail conditions excellent.
Snow gone below 9,000 ft. Above that it's patchy, easy to follow the trail with a GPS.
Glissade chute on the north side is icy, not safe to slide today.
Trail open again after the fire closure, burned area has lots of loose ash and some dead snags.
Cairns knocked down in the boulder field, route finding was tricky in the fog.
High water on the Sucker Brook crossing, rock hop impossible today. Wet feet guaranteed.
Turned around at the col, whiteout conditions and the trail was invisible in fresh snow.
Lower loop is flooded, upper loop dry. Parking lot plowed.
Took the Beaver Brook trail, the cascades section had verglas all over. Very slow going.
Trail runners heads up: new bridge on the east loop is open, no more wet crossing.
The avalanche danger on the approach is considerable today, we skinned the ridge instead of the gully.
Groomed Nordic loops at the park are in great shape this morning, fresh corduroy on the upper trails.
Ski trail report: the black run under the lift is scraped to ice, blue runs soft and fun by 11.
ATV trail system reopened after the mud season closure, still a few soft spots in the low sections.
The OHV route over the pass has a snowdrift at the top, not passable for side by sides yet.
Bike trail is tacky and fast after the rain, a couple of new roots exposed on the descent.
Climbing report: the approach trail to the crag is fine but the base is soaked, rock dry by noon.
Horse trail at the state forest has deep ruts after the storm, riders should avoid the creek loop.
Via ferrata cables were rimed with ice this morning, route closed until it melts off.
Snowshoed the summer trail today, about two feet of powder, breaking trail was exhausting.
Two hikers rescued yesterday after sliding on the snowfield. Please carry traction and an axe.
Trail through the burn is open but downed trees every hundred yards, expect lots of stepping over.
Leaves are covering the rocks and roots on the ridge, easy to twist an ankle. Watch your footing.
Hot and exposed on the canyon trail, no shade after 9am. Heat advisory in effect.
Water on the trail everywhere from the spring melt, the low section is a creek right now.
The boardwalk near the bog is broken in a few places, step carefully.
Summited today. Trail marked with orange blazes all the way, only a few icy spots near the top.
Flash flood warning for the slot canyons today, rangers closed the Narrows at the Temple.
Early season conditions on the ridge: snow patches, cornices still hanging over the east side.
Horseflies and heat but the trail itself is in excellent condition, recently brushed out.
Big washout on the trail below the falls, detour marked through the woods.
Trail was busy but in good shape. Dry, fast, no snow, the summit sign is back up.
Aux sommets aujourd'hui, le sentier est glacé au-dessus de la limite des arbres. Crampons obligatoires.
Sentier du Mont-Albert fermé ce matin à cause des vents forts, selon le poste d'accueil.
Beaucoup de boue sur le sentier des Crêtes, et plusieurs arbres tombés après la tempête.
La passerelle sur la rivière est emportée, le passage à gué est dangereux avec la fonte.
Neige au-dessus de 900 m, raquettes utiles, la trace n'est pas encore faite.
Conditions du sentier : sec jusqu'au belvédère, puis glace sur les rochers au sommet.
Stationnement du sentier plein dès 8 h ce samedi, prévoyez d'arriver tôt.
Les moustiques sont terribles au lac, mais le sentier est en excellent état.
Pistes de ski de fond damées ce matin, conditions excellentes sur les boucles du haut.
Chute de pierres sur le sentier près du col, faites attention.
Subimos al volcán hoy. Mucha nieve arriba de los 3,000 m, hay que llevar crampones.
El sendero al lago está cerrado por incendio, lo anunciaron los guardaparques esta mañana.
Cuidado, el puente del arroyo se cayó con la tormenta y el cruce está muy crecido.
Hay árboles caídos en todo el sendero después del viento de ayer, se puede pasar pero lento.
El estacionamiento del sendero se llenó a las 7, mucha gente estacionada en la carretera.
Barro hasta los tobillos en la parte baja del sendero, arriba está seco.
Hielo en las rocas cerca de la cumbre esta mañana, subimos con bastones y crampones.
Reporte del sendero: sin nieve hasta el paso, mucho viento en la cresta.
Hay víboras de cascabel cerca del segundo mirador, tengan cuidado.
El camino de terracería al inicio del sendero está deslavado, hay que caminar dos kilómetros más.
